text:
**Short version:** Qi2 and Qi2.2 are open standards from the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC). MagSafe is Apple's branded version of the same idea. Qi2.2 is the faster of the two standards.

| | Qi2 | Qi2.2 (Qi2 25W) | MagSafe |
|---|---|---|---|
| Who owns it | WPC | WPC | Apple |
| Max speed | 15W | 25W | 25W on iPhone 16 and later, 15W on older iPhones |
| Magnets | Yes | Yes | Yes |

**Qi2:** This added a magnetic ring to Qi so the phone and charger line up, which improves efficiency. Apple contributed MagSafe technology to the standard. It is capped at 15W ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)).

**Qi2.2:** The WPC markets this as "Qi2 25W." It delivers nearly 70% more power than Qi2 and can charge a phone from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)). The first products were certified in July 2025. You only get 25W if the phone supports it. Examples are the iPhone 16 and later and the Pixel 10 Pro XL. Other phones fall back to 15W ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).

**MagSafe:** This is Apple's magnet-and-charging system, supported by iPhone 12 and later (not the iPhone SE or 16e). Apple's own MagSafe Charger is certified for Qi2 25W and Qi, so it also works with other Qi devices and AirPods with a wireless charging case ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m?fnode=7120d2e211c5d2008372acfadfa9b649c5ec92879b07e2f040e38952fcd8be0794ade18a93d927b4c96c7a13cda2597927c0814a65dc0189e774b77c7fdb7e748fe7efe26c0c6c21f59929ac37012aa0ac916746c2f56a8e6448ccdb97e7d384&fs=s%3Dnewest%26fh%3D8e12f5%252B81eaf8)). Apple's support page says:
- 25W needs a 30W or greater adapter and an iPhone 17 or 18 series, or a 16 Plus or 16 Pro Max.
- The iPhone 16 and 16 Pro get about 22.5W, and the iPhone Air gets 20W.
- The iPhone 17e and iPhone 15 and earlier get up to 15W ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047)).

**Watch for "MagSafe-compatible":** Macworld notes that uncertified chargers with this label are usually just 7.5W with magnets to hold the phone in place. Certified ones are 15W or 25W. Certified MagSafe chargers also include an NFC antenna so the iPhone can identify them, plus a magnetometer to prevent compass interference ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)).

**Android:** Support is thin. Pixel 10, 10 Pro and 10 Pro Fold do Qi2 at 15W. Samsung's Galaxy S26 lineup is "Qi2 Ready," which means 15W only with a magnetic case ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).

**What to buy:**
- **iPhone 16 or newer:** Choose a Qi2.2 or Apple MagSafe charger to get 25W. [Apple MagSafe Charger (2 m)](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m?fnode=7120d2e211c5d2008372acfadfa9b649c5ec92879b07e2f040e38952fcd8be0794ade18a93d927b4c96c7a13cda2597927c0814a65dc0189e774b77c7fdb7e748fe7efe26c0c6c21f59929ac37012aa0ac916746c2f56a8e6448ccdb97e7d384&fs=s%3Dnewest%26fh%3D8e12f5%252B81eaf8) is $49. Macworld lists the 1 m version at $39.
- **iPhone 12 to 15, or an older Qi2 phone:** A 15W Qi2 charger is enough. A 25W charger works too, but your phone limits it to 15W.
- **Power bank:** The Verge's testing found the [Baseus PicoGo AM52 Qi2.2 power bank](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w) charged fastest wirelessly. It took an iPhone 17 Pro Max to 65% in an hour. Dealectric lists it at $59.99, or $53.99 with code AM52. That link is a commission link, so Dealectric earns a fee if you buy through it, at no extra cost to you. The Verge saw it at $60 to $70 elsewhere.

To confirm a charger is really certified, search the WPC's product database from [their Qi page](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/).
